title: Spare Parts Halo
style: Eclectic jazz with a laid-back swung pocket, неож? no English only. Better: Eclectic jazz with brushed drums, walking bass, off-kilter piano clusters, and guitar skitters; verse rides sparse bass and piano, pre-chorus opens with clipped horn replies, chorus blooms into a loose unison riff. Close-mic vocal with sly doubles and short scat ad-libs, tape hiss, reversed cymbal swells, and brushed fills between lines. Bright, roomy, and slightly mischievous mix., eclectic, jazz
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I came in with the bent-back tie
Scuffed shoes, loud grin, side-eye pride
Everybody moved like one gray wave
I cut a corner, took the brave

My laugh hit wrong, then hit just right
Like a match in a darkened room at night
You can fold your arms, look away
I still leave a mark in the sway

[Pre-Chorus]
Too clean, too neat
Too safe, too small
I hear my name
Bouncing off the wall

[Chorus]
I stick out
I stick out
Like a bright red thread
In a charcoal crowd

I stick out
I stick out
You can try to blend
I was born too loud

[Verse 2]
Gold ring tapping on the glass
I talk too fast, let the seconds pass
Got a polka-dot thought and a crooked plan
A little bit spark, a little bit stand

They wore the script, I bent the page
Not for the crowd, not for the stage
But when the room goes pale and thin
I’m the weird little light they lean on in

[Pre-Chorus]
Too clean, too neat
Too safe, too small
I hear my name
Bouncing off the wall

[Chorus]
I stick out
I stick out
Like a bright red thread
In a charcoal crowd

I stick out
I stick out
You can try to blend
I was born too loud

[Bridge]
And if the room turns cool
I bring my own heat
A crooked little smile
And a syncopated beat

Let them wear the mask
Let them keep the line
I’d rather be the odd note
Than disappear in time

[Chorus]
I stick out
I stick out
Like a bright red thread
In a charcoal crowd

I stick out
I stick out
You can try to blend
I was born too loud

[Outro]
Bend, don't break
Blink, don't hide
I fit best
On the outside
